The main risks are unsafe URL construction, weak response/schema validation, incomplete typed-package packaging, and batch behavior that can silently lose or mis-handle API results.

issues.description: Resource IDs are interpolated directly into URL paths, allowing malformed IDs or path/query injection to target the wrong endpoint.
Batch-create silently drops non-object result entries instead of failing, which can hide partial data loss.
Pagination silently ignores malformed item entries and treats missing items as an empty page.
Network and timeout exceptions from httpx are not wrapped in the client's typed exception hierarchy.
Retry-After handling only accepts numeric seconds, ignores standard HTTP-date values, and has no maximum sleep cap.
batch_create materializes the entire iterable and all results in memory, contradicting the any-number chunking claim for large inputs.
API model constructors trust enum-like fields and required keys without clear validation errors or schema-level checks.
Task subclasses TaskCreate, so read models can be passed to batch_create and serialized with server-owned id/state fields.
The package advertises typed models but does not include a py.typed marker for downstream type checkers.
httpx dependency has no upper bound, making future major-version breakage possible.
max_attempts is not validated, so zero or negative values produce misleading request-was-not-attempted errors.
Frozen dataclasses expose mutable dict fields, so model instances are not actually immutable.
Public literal type aliases such as ReviewVerdict are used in signatures but not re-exported from the package root.
Tests miss important failure cases: URL encoding, malformed responses, network errors, schema validation, and large iterable behavior.
